title: Trump, Xi, and the Race for Superintelligence
gist: Podcast listing in which CNAS adjunct senior fellow Jordan Schneider of ChinaTalk discusses US versus China approaches to AI, the Trump-Xi summit, censorship limits on Chinese AI models, and why Chinese public opinion on AI is more positive than American opinion. The page also teases CNAS commentary arguing the Trump-Xi summit left Taiwan in limbo.

insights.claim: Many people in China hold positive expectations for AI while Americans are markedly more pessimistic, a public-opinion gap that Jordan Schneider discusses with Jerusalem Demsas and Matt Yglesias.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Divergent public sentiment may translate into faster AI adoption and lighter political resistance in China than in the US.
insights.quote: why do so many people in China have positive expectations for AI while Americans are dooming?

insights.claim: Chinese AI models face limits on what they are allowed to say, a constraint discussed alongside how the US and China differ in their approaches to AI.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Censorship constraints may shape the global competitiveness of Chinese models outside China.

insights.claim: CNAS's Derek Grossman argues Xi used the Trump-Xi summit to signal the change Beijing wants on Taiwan, which Trump did not publicly grant, leaving Taiwan in limbo.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Ambiguity in US Taiwan policy after the summit is a lingering geopolitical risk for Taiwan-exposed assets.
insights.quote: Xi used the summit to mark the change Beijing wants. Trump did not publicly grant it.
insights.locator: The Trump-Xi Summit Leaves Taiwan in Limbo

insights.claim: A CNAS commentary by David Feith frames the nuclear race as a choice between an integrated American system combining public missions with private capital and a fragmented one facing China's coordinated buildup.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Points to a policy push for public-private capital partnerships in US nuclear buildout.
insights.quote: The choice is between an integrated American system that combines public missions with private capital and a fragmented one facing off against China’s coordinated buildup.
insights.locator: America’s Secret Weapon in the Nuclear Race

top_entities: Center for a New American Security
